Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
45-year-old female housekeeper with 3–4 month history of painful, cracked, itchy palms likely secondary to occupational contact dermatitis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Soreness, cracking, and intermittent itch of palmar skin for 3–4 months; recently worsened, limiting ability to work.  
• Associated symptoms: Occasional bleeding when scratched; generalized mild skin dryness (legs). Denies fever, GI or urinary symptoms, nausea/vomiting. Appetite normal.  
• Pertinent negatives: No prior eczema or dermatitis.  
• PMH: Type 2 diabetes.  
• Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented). OTC E45 emollient and antihistamine trial—minimal benefit.  
• Allergies: None reported.  
• Family history: Diabetes; no known skin disorders.  
• Social: Housekeeper in a hotel; frequent exposure to cleaning chemicals; often does not wear gloves. Non-smoker. Alcohol: “couple of pints” weekly.  

Examination:
(No examination or vitals documented.)

Impression:
Occupational contact (irritant) dermatitis of the hands.

Plan:
• Education: Avoid irritants; wear protective gloves at all times while cleaning.  
• Medications prescribed:  
  – Topical corticosteroid cream (specific formulation/dose not documented).  
  – High-strength emollient; apply generously 3–4 times daily for 2 weeks.  
• Follow-up: Re-evaluate in 10–14 days; return sooner if worsening or spreading occurs. Prescription sent to patient’s pharmacy.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Physical examination, vitals, current HbA1c or diabetes control status, complete medication reconciliation (only metformin noted), immunization status.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational noise, no major inaudible segments.
